I have been working this land since I was a boy. Sixty years tells you things no school ever could. My body knows the rhythm of wheat in winter and maize in summer. That is what I do. That is what my father did.

This year is no different. My 10.2 mu — I keep 7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, same as always. The other 3.2 mu I put in stevia. The stevia buyer comes every autumn. It brings cash. Two of us in the house, we do not need more land than we can manage ourselves.

**Wheat (winter):** I plant in mid-October after the maize comes off. I use the improved seed from the supply cooperative — not the old seed I saved, because the improved variety gives me more grain and stands up better to the wind. Before planting I do rotary tillage to break up the soil from maize roots. I put down diammonium phosphate and a little potassium as base fertilizer before I till it in, then I top-dress urea at jointing in late March. I irrigate four times: once in late November to help the seedlings through cold, once at jointing, once at heading, once as the grain fills. I spray twice — once early for weeds, once at heading for aphids and rust. I expect around 450 jin per mu, maybe 480 if the spring rains come right.

**Maize (summer):** Right after wheat harvest in June I rotary-till and plant hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses hybrid. I have used it for thirty years. I put fertilizer down at planting and top-dress again when the plants are knee-high. I water twice — once if it is dry at planting, once at silking if there is no rain. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide early, then I watch for aphids and corn borer. I get around 550 jin per mu most years.

**Stevia (spring/summer):** I plough this plot in April, deeper than rotary. Stevia roots need room. I plant cuttings I kept from last year's crop. I do not push it with too much nitrogen — it makes leaves, not grain, so I keep nitrogen lower and give it more water through summer. I irrigate four times through the dry months. I spray once or twice for insects. The buyer wants dry leaf, I get around 100 jin per mu.

I do not change what works.
